summary.headline: Rust is ready for inference, search, vision, documents and numerics; scale-out training and RL still pull you back to Python.
summary.summary: Ship in Rust for LLM serving, search, document extraction, speech, classical ML and numerics. Inference is the strongest ground: servers and embeddable engines do the work in Rust with no C or C++ engine requirement. Weaker: object detection and segmentation mostly go through ONNX Runtime wrappers, and office-document conversion still wraps native OCR and PDF code. Training on one GPU is real; cross-machine sharding and reinforcement-learning tooling are thin, and experiment tracking is absent. Python stays for optional weight conversion, a few Python-only APIs and RL libraries. Tokenization, Arrow and Parquet, Safetensors and GGUF are solid.

jobs.verdict: Serving leads: [[candle-vllm]] and [[blazr]] ship OpenAI-compatible servers; [[furnace]] ships a pure-Rust server from a library. [[mistralrs]] embeds quantized LLMs, pure Rust by default. [[tract]], [[rten]] and [[oxionnx]] run ONNX in Rust; [[ort]] wraps native ONNX Runtime.

[[rig]] and [[swiftide]] cover agents, tools, RAG, tracing; [[rmcp]] is the official MCP SDK; [[yoagent]] is an explicit agent loop; [[rstructor]] forces schema output; [[async-openai]] and [[rust-genai]] call hosted APIs. Limit: API churn; replay is framework-specific.

[[burn]] and [[candle]] train on one GPU with autodiff and custom layers; [[rumus]] adds multi-GPU and FSDP; [[oxidizr]] runs full LLM training loops with checkpoints; [[rust-autograd]] is focused AD. Limit: no maintained Rust RL algorithm or trainer, and cross-machine sharding is thin.

[[transcribe-rs]] and [[parakeet-rs]] transcribe, [[any-tts]] and [[xn-ptts]] synthesize, [[earshot]] does streaming VAD in pure Rust, [[speakrs]] diarizes, [[voxr]] decodes and resamples. Every listed need has a Rust path; several engines wrap ONNX Runtime or whisper.cpp.

[[tokenizers]], [[splintr]] and [[kitoken]] match model families, [[fastembed-rs]] and [[model2vec-rs]] embed locally, [[qdrant]], [[lancedb]] and [[tantivy]] cover vector and full-text search, [[meilisearch]] serves hybrid. Limit: [[rust-bert]] tagging and NER wraps LibTorch.

[[kornia-rs]] and [[imageproc]] decode and transform images in Rust; [[aha]] runs vision, OCR and segmentation on Candle; [[cake]] generates images; [[kornia-slam]] does visual-inertial SLAM. Limit: detection and segmentation mainly come from [[usls]] and [[inference]], which wrap ONNX Runtime.

[[vidr]] decodes NVDEC, Vulkan Video and CPU codecs into tensors, runs restore models, encodes and muxes; [[containr]] reads and writes MP4/MKV; [[rav1r]] is the Rust AV1 encoder. Limit: no CPU HEVC or VP9 encode, no VA-API, no fragmented MP4 input, early releases.

[[ocrs]] and [[franken-ocr]] read scans in Rust, [[pdf-oxide]] extracts PDF text, [[oxidizepdf]] chunks PDFs for retrieval, [[edgeparse]] handles tables and reading order. Limit: office formats rely on [[docling]], [[xberg]] and [[kreuzberg-lts]], which wrap native OCR and PDF libraries.

[[smartcore]] and [[linfa]] cover regression, SVM, forests and clustering; [[perpetual]] boosts trees with SHAP explanations, [[treeboost]] trains GBDT on CUDA and WebGPU; [[augurs]] forecasts and finds changepoints; [[rust-automl]] compares models. Limit: early APIs, and [[egobox]] documents a Python-only entry point.

[[ndarray]] is the array base; [[faer]] and [[nalgebra]] do linear algebra; [[rustfft]] and [[ndrustfft]] FFT; [[sprs]] sparse; [[statrs]] and [[ndarray-stats]] statistics; [[argmin]], [[basin]] and [[pounce]] optimize; [[differential-equations]] solves ODE and PDE; [[scirs]] covers signals and spatial work.

[[burn]], [[candle]] and [[numr]] run tensor math on GPU with autodiff; [[cubecl]] compiles one Rust kernel to CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU and CPU; [[boostr]] adds attention and quantization. Limit: early APIs, WebGPU is F32-only in places, and [[cubecl]] is alpha.

[[safetensors]] and [[gguf]] handle model files; [[arrow-rs]], [[polars]] and [[datafusion]] cover columnar data; [[hdf5-pure]], [[zarrs]] and [[ndarray-npy]] read array formats; [[hf-hub]] downloads from the Hub; [[lance]] and [[vortex]] add lakehouse formats.

use_now.why: Rust server with OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama routes, streaming, GGUF, SafeTensors, AWQ and GPTQ. One-person project, and audio needs a C library.

use_now.use_for: Embed quantized LLMs in a Rust app
use_now.why: Engine with GGUF, structured output, tool calling, LoRA, embeddings and agents, and a default build needing no C compiler or system libraries.

use_now.use_for: General Rust tensor and model work
use_now.why: Small framework with CUDA and Metal backends and transformer, vision and audio examples that teams reuse daily.
Autodiff, ONNX import and CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan and WebGPU backends in one framework with no Python runtime.
Rust server with dense, sparse and hybrid search, filtering, sharding and replication. Ships as a service, not a crate.
Rust library with BM25, incremental indexing and facet fields; the engine several search servers build on.
Rust implementation of normalization, pre-tokenization and BPE or WordPiece, with loading and training of tokenizer files.

use_now.use_for: Agents, tools and RAG in Rust
use_now.why: One library for providers, tools, vector stores, MCP and effect replay, with hundreds of teams building on it.
Official Rust Model Context Protocol SDK with tools, resources, prompts, OAuth and transport options.
Zero-copy reads, bf16 and fp8 support, and the format nearly every Rust inference path expects.
Arrow-based engine with lazy queries and streaming, usable from Rust without the Python bindings.
Broad supervised and unsupervised coverage, native Rust with no wrapped library, defaults targeting WASM.

watch.why: Serves Burn and ONNX models over KServe and OpenAI routes from one Rust server. Early releases, no long production record, few GPU measurements.
Compiles ONNX graphs to specialized Rust for embedded and WASM, with ASR, VAD and vision examples. No Loop support and only partial Einsum.

watch.use_for: ONNX inference with no C runtime
watch.why: Pure-Rust ONNX engine with control flow and quantization. No tokenizer or sampling controls, and GPU providers are not fully verified.
Streams from seven LLM protocols, runs tools, sessions and sub-agents on native and WASM. No vector stores, embeddings or task graph.
One Rust kernel compiles to CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU and CPU. Alpha, no tensor cores on WebGPU, platform features differ.

watch.use_for: Video decode and restore on GPU tensors
watch.why: Frames as GPU tensors plus restoration models and encoding. Early, no VA-API, no CPU HEVC or VP9 encode.

build_today.goal: Self-hosted LLM service behind an OpenAI-compatible API
build_today.why: [[candle-vllm]] serves OpenAI routes with streaming, continuous batching and paged attention; [[hf-hub]] pulls weights; [[safetensors]] reads them. No Python runtime.
build_today.watch_out: CUDA and Metal only, and no crate release; auth, rate limits and throughput tuning are your code.

build_today.goal: Q&A over private documents with local embeddings
build_today.why: [[rig]] supplies the agent and vector-store wiring, [[fastembed-rs]] embeds locally, [[qdrant]] stores and searches, [[oxidizepdf]] and [[pdf-oxide]] turn PDFs into text and retrieval chunks in Rust.
build_today.watch_out: Rig APIs move between releases; chunking strategy and answer quality remain your work.

build_today.goal: On-device meeting transcription with speaker labels
build_today.why: [[voxr]] decodes and resamples audio in Rust, [[earshot]] finds speech in the stream, [[lele]] compiles ASR graphs into Rust, [[speakrs]] assigns speakers and emits RTTM.
build_today.watch_out: [[lele]] lacks Loop and has partial Einsum, so check your model compiles; [[speakrs]] needs a backend feature and rejects arbitrary ONNX on native CPU.

build_today.goal: Document intake service turning scans and PDFs into chunks
build_today.why: [[ocrs]] reads scans, [[pdf-oxide]] and [[edgeparse]] extract text, tables and reading order, [[oxidizepdf]] emits structure-aware chunks, [[tantivy]] indexes them for search.
build_today.watch_out: The pure-Rust paths have no learned layout model, so table accuracy trails hosted pipelines.

build_today.goal: Forecasting and risk service over tabular data
build_today.why: [[augurs]] covers forecasting, seasonality and changepoint detection, [[perpetual]] boosts trees with SHAP explanations, [[smartcore]] supplies classic estimators.
build_today.watch_out: All early releases, and there is no Rust experiment-tracking UI, so log metrics and checkpoints yourself.

holes_filled.hole: Quantized LLM inference and OpenAI-compatible serving without a C engine
holes_filled.note: Teams can ship a model endpoint from Rust alone. Python can go for serving; only optional model conversion still uses it.

holes_filled.hole: Vector, full-text and hybrid search in one Rust stack
holes_filled.note: Database, library and server options all exist. Python leaves the retrieval path; embedding quality is your choice of model.

holes_filled.hole: Speech pipeline: VAD, transcription, diarization, synthesis, audio decode
holes_filled.note: Every speech need has a working Rust path. Some engines wrap ONNX Runtime or whisper.cpp, so check the binary you ship.

holes_filled.hole: Scanned PDFs and images to text, tables and retrieval chunks
holes_filled.note: Pure-Rust extraction covers text, tables, reading order and structure-aware chunks. Office formats still route through native-backed libraries.

holes_filled.hole: Classical ML on tables with explanations and forecasting
holes_filled.note: Regression, boosting, SHAP and time-series forecasting are all available. Python can go unless you need its experiment tooling.

holes_filled.hole: NumPy and SciPy work: arrays, linear algebra, FFT, statistics, optimization
holes_filled.note: Core numerics are pure Rust. Python leaves the numerical path; optional plotting in some crates still pulls in matplotlib.

holes_filled.hole: Exact tokenization for the main model families
holes_filled.note: Token ids match the reference implementations, so preprocessing no longer needs a Python service.

holes_open.hole: A maintained Rust reinforcement-learning stack: algorithms, trainers, replay
holes_open.impact: Stops teams building RL products in Rust; only environment tooling exists, so the agent and training loop are yours or Python's.
holes_open.workaround: Write the loop on [[burn]] or [[candle]], or train in a Python RL library and port the policy.

holes_open.hole: Cross-machine sharded training with FSDP, ZeRO or pipeline parallelism
holes_open.impact: Stops teams training large models across nodes in Rust; distributed support stops at one machine or bare collectives.
holes_open.workaround: Use [[nexar]] for collectives and write sharding yourself, or train in Python and export weights.

holes_open.hole: General multi-object tracking for arbitrary video
holes_open.impact: Stops video analytics teams from tracking objects across frames; only SLAM-style camera motion is covered by a maintained crate.
holes_open.workaround: Reimplement trackers on top of detection output, or call an external library and keep the pipeline in Rust.

holes_open.hole: Full codec coverage for video encode in Rust
holes_open.impact: Stops a pure-Rust transcoder: CPU HEVC and VP9 encode and AMD or Intel Vulkan Video decode are missing.
holes_open.workaround: Encode AV1 with [[rav1r]] or use NVENC, and shell out to a native encoder for the rest.

holes_open.hole: Experiment tracking with dashboards and comparison
holes_open.impact: Stops teams from comparing runs inside Rust; checkpoints and metrics exist per framework, but no maintained tracker row.
holes_open.workaround: Log to files or OpenTelemetry and view results in an external tool.

holes_open.hole: Mixed office files to structured text without native PDF and OCR libraries
holes_open.impact: Stops a pure-Rust document pipeline for Office formats; [[docling]], [[xberg]] and [[kreuzberg-lts]] cover them but wrap native PDFium, OCR and ONNX Runtime.
holes_open.workaround: Ship the wrapper and accept the native build, or keep PDFs and scans in Rust with [[ocrs]], [[pdf-oxide]] and [[oxidizepdf]] and convert Office files separately.

charts.takeaway: Rust ML includes pure-Rust and native-wrapped implementations, so teams must verify whether safety and portability come from Rust or from underlying native code.
GPU support is fragmented and often unknown, so teams should verify backend coverage for their target hardware instead of assuming portability.
Release activity is mixed, with many recent shipments alongside a stale tail, so teams should check maintenance cadence before adopting a dependency.
